source.title: Abstraction Mechanisms Predict Generalization in Deep Neural Networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present, though some figure values are not provided as text.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how a different property, CNA, relates to train–test generalization gaps and compares it with norm- and margin-based metrics. Its own results bear on the broader question of which measured properties track the gap, but it does not test the specific magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CNA correlations with test performance and with train–test gaps. Figure 7 gives the gap-correlation results only graphically; exact values are not stated. The Gaussian-noise dataset is described as being memorized, but the text does not state its held-out accuracy.
record.test_reason: The study uses random-data memorization to stress-test its CNA-Margin metric and reports that metric's performance. It does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or any other specified version. Natural-label versus random-label held-out performance under matched recipes is not reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. More precisely, the authors distinguish CNA's association with test performance from CNA-Margin's prediction of train–test gaps, and report advantages over tested norm- and margin-based metrics, especially with dataset corruption. They encourage further investigation; the results do not establish causality.
record.recipe_differences: Measures CNA and CNA-Margin rather than the magnitude-aware sharpness measure described in V7; evaluates correlations with train–test gaps across datasets and architectures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparisons include Gaussian-noise data and varying label corruption from 10% to 50%; CNA-Margin is described as comparatively robust in these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that CNA-Margin correlates with train–test gaps comparatively robustly when Gaussian random data or partially shuffled training labels are included; numerical correlations are not available in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CNA-Margin predicts generalization gaps across varied datasets and architectures, with greater robustness to dataset corruption than the tested norm- and margin-based metrics.

record.problems: The central gap-correlation results are presented graphically without numerical values in the text. The authors describe the evaluation as empirical and say the early experiments do not warrant broad conclusions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted. Figure 7 presents correlations conditional on each architecture as well as aggregate correlations, but the text does not state their individual values; rows retain the stated aggregate findings for the two described corruption conditions.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fixed random-label training fits and held-out accuracies; random-label held-out accuracy at chance.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Evaluating another generalization metric against norm- and margin-based baselines does not test V7's specific sharpness claim. The stated memorization of random Gaussian training data supplies no matched held-out comparison sufficient for V1.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not compare natural-label and random-label held-out performance for the same architectures and training recipes.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the interpolation threshold is reported.
Architectures are included in a broad evaluation, but the study does not compare convolutional and fully connected models to test their relative generalization.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison is reported.
The study evaluates CNA and CNA-Margin, not magnitude-aware sharpness or weight-perturbation tolerance.
No memorized-example removal or retraining comparison is reported.

rows.subject: All Nets
rows.operation_detail: Correlated CNA-Margin and other generalization metrics with train–test generalization gaps across the evaluated networks, including a Gaussian-noise dataset.

conditions.value: ImageNet, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and Gaussian noise
All architectures in aggregate; analyzed every 20 training epochs

rows.measure: Pearson correlation of CNA-Margin with the train–test generalization gap
rows.note: The text says norm-based metrics perform very poorly on the Gaussian-noise dataset while CNA-Margin remains comparatively robust; exact correlations are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: CNA-Margin correlation does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. Numerical correlations are unavailable in the supplied figure text. The architecture is ResNet-101 in the main text but ResNet-100 in the Figure 7 caption; the discrepancy should be recorded.

conditions.value: ImageNet, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST
All architectures in aggregate and conditional on architecture; analyzed every 20 training epochs

rows.measure: Pearson correlation of CNA-Margin with the train–test generalization gap

Section 4.3 says only a subset of networks underwent label corruption, so the listed architectures and datasets should not imply every combination was evaluated.
